note: Gold corpus for the resolver. `simt skills eval` reads this file (a path argument names a different one) and reports precision and recall against it; `test/eval.test.mjs` runs the same scoring through the shared module in `src/resolve/eval.mjs`. It lives under test/ because test data does not ship in the package: an installed copy says so instead of scoring the author's.
whyFixtureNotRepo: Each case declares the repository SIGNALS rather than staging a directory, because what is being pinned is the resolver: given these repo facts and this task, these are the right skills. `fingerprint` has its own tests, and a corpus that also exercised it would fail with a resolver bug inside it and send the next reader to the wrong file.

cases.name: a D1 migration in a Workers repo picks the platform skill
cases.why: Review 0001 section S04 acceptance, verbatim. `d1` is a keyword only `cloudflare` declares, so the keyword signal is the whole selection. The reject list is the other half of the same acceptance: `wrangler` scores 8 on its summary alone and must stay out, and the two skills that are compatible with this repo but irrelevant to the task prove the stack gate is not a selector.

cases.name: a task made of stopwords selects nothing
cases.why: The other half of the same acceptance. Before the minimum score this resolved four skills on `summary:the` and `summary:in`.
cases.task: fix a typo in the README

cases.name: two overlapping stack tags are compatibility, not evidence
cases.why: Stack is 15 a tag, so this repo alone scores any skill declaring two of them 30 - above the minimum. Only a rule that excludes stack from its own threshold rejects them.

cases.name: a changed file selects on the path, whatever the task says
cases.why: Path is weight 100 and is ground truth. The task here is close to meaningless, and the skill should still be found.
cases.caveat: `cloudflare` and `workers-best-practices` declare the same path and are selected too, and this case is not asserting otherwise: a path is evidence for every skill that claims it, and which of the three bodies the reader needs is a budget question, not a ranking one.

cases.name: a Gradle repo never sees the Cloudflare reference
cases.why: Pure gate, kept because the new minimum score makes it easy to confuse a low score with a rejected one. The stack gate still excludes, and now also reports why. Guards the gate against the selection rule: the rule must not become a second, weaker gate.

cases.name: sign-in in a Firebase repo
cases.why: `sign in` is a multi-word keyword, so this also carries S03's phrase matching into the corpus rather than leaving it to one unit test.

cases.name: a deploy task in a Workers repo
cases.why: `deploy` is a capability alias for `release`, which only `wrangler` declares, so the capability signal selects it; the keyword `deploy` confirms. The other platform skills score on `worker` alone and are not asserted against: a capability hit is exactly what the minimum score admits.

cases.name: a durable object task in a Workers repo
cases.why: The phrase `durable object` is declared on two skills, so both are selected and only the one it names is asserted: the keyword is the declaration, and a corpus that argued with the registry's own declaration would be a second registry.

cases.name: an anti-pattern task in a Workers repo
cases.why: `floating promise` is a keyword only `workers-best-practices` declares. A skill whose every keyword is a phrase is the case where a token-equality matcher would select nothing.

cases.name: a knowledge graph task in a Node repo
cases.why: Three keywords of `graphify` fire on one task, which is the case where the keyword signal must not saturate: each declared keyword scores once, and the summary words that share the task's words add 8 apiece on top.

cases.name: a simt command task in a Node repo
cases.why: The tool's own reference skill selects on its name and its keywords; the Firebase skills are compatible with this repo through `node` and must stay out on evidence, not on the gate.
cases.task: which simt command runs the gates

cases.name: a firebase init task in a Firebase repo
cases.why: `init` and `project` are keywords only `firebase-basics` declares; `firebase-auth-basics` is selected on the shared `firebase` keyword and is not asserted against, for the same reason as the durable object case.
